Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a right-sided, slightly lobulated mass in the superior mediastinum with increased retrotracheal soft-tissue density on the lateral view, which is characteristic of a mediastinal lipoma (fat-density lesion). Unlike neurofibromas or carcinomas, lipomas typically present as well-circumscribed, non-invasive masses with fat attenuation that can be identified by their specific radiographic appearance in the mediastinum.
